An implementation may optionally provide the elements specified in Annex A, Communications facility
shall accept the syntax and provide the functionality for all standard language elements required by this International Standard
only when support for that language element is claimed by the implementor

cases.reason: 2002 makes exactly one element optional, Annex A (communications facility, §2002:3.1); VALIDATE is clause 14.8.46, a normative element of clauses 6-16 that §2002:3.1 and §2002:3.1.1 require, and it is not in the 2002 B.3 processor-dependent list either. The 2023 DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT rests on §2023:A.4.1/A.4.14 (VALIDATE an OPTIONAL element), a licence the 2002 text does not contain. At --std 2002 the compiler accepts VALIDATE inert with warning COBOL1580, whose own text cites §2023:4.2.7 / Annex A.4.14 as its licence, and refuses the validation clauses (VALIDATE-STATUS, DEFAULT, DESTINATION, CLASS, INVALID...) by name with COBOL1708. The 2002 requirement (perform the validation) is not met, so the 2023 verdict cannot carry. Format and rule words are otherwise identical (2023 adds message-tag to SR2 and a new SR6, neither in this pair). Because the clause is refused wholesale, the rule's own check is never reached.
cases.needs: 2002 requires the VALIDATE statement (and its data-division clauses); the compiler declines it at --std 2002

cases.reason: The rule picks the declarative by the FIRST exception in the statement's order of evaluation, so it defers to the rules that decide which exceptions a statement raises and in what order. In 2002 that includes statements under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD (OPTIONS paragraph), where a value too large for a standard intermediate data item (32 digits, magnitude up to 9.99...E+999) sets EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW, and exponentiation is evaluated before division. 2023 removed standard arithmetic (E.2 item 21), so the 2023 row's evidence (pb3261, pb370) never exercises it. Probe gr11std.cob: COMPUTE X = 10 ** T + 1 / Z (T=1000, Z=0) with handlers for EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW and EC-SIZE-ZERO-DIVIDE. 2002 requires EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW to be the first exception. At --std 2002 the compiler selects EC-SIZE-ZERO-DIVIDE. gr11ovf.cob (10 ** T alone) shows no overflow is raised at all, only EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION on the store. The root is the known standard-intermediate defect (2002 8.8.1.3.1: 34-digit decimal used where 2002 sets 32 digits and a 1E+1000 ceiling); this is a rule it reaches.
